title: Captured simulation phase
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $c_0$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$, and let $t$ be a natural number. Suppose that $M$ is not halted at any time $j<t$ when run from $c_0$. Then the clean wrapper, run for $t$ steps from the captured logged version of $c_0$ with empty captured prefix and output, is in the captured logged configuration corresponding to the time-$t$ configuration of $M$ and the history of its first $t$ steps, with empty captured prefix and output.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
$c_0$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $x$
the run of $M$ from $c_0$ is not halted at every time $j<t$
replaced:
If a source machine $M$ is live for $t$ steps from a configuration $c_0$, then the
clean wrapper of $M$, run for $t$ steps from the captured logged start of $c_0$,
reaches the captured logged configuration of $M$'s time-$t$ configuration with the
$t$-step history; any halting emission of $M$ is retained on the capture tape.
